identity.description: Two-part count mixture: a logit/probit INFLATION submodel decides whether a row is a structural zero (never-participant), and a Poisson/NB COUNT submodel generates counts (including sampling zeros) otherwise. Separates 'won't ever' from 'didn't this time' — two coefficient stories one plain count model conflates.

consumes.note: non-negative integer count target with excess zeros; exog_infl (inflation design) defaults to the same matrix but may be a subset

emits.note: expected count = (1 - pi) * lambda, the mixture mean; the fitted two-part model defines the full zero-inflated predictive distribution

pi = P(structural zero | x) from the inflation submodel — a per-row probability, though of a latent regime rather than a class label; closest existing port (pi derived as 1 - prob-main; prob-main returns the COUNT-regime probability, not pi)
TWO blocks: inflation (logit/probit) coefficients and count (log-linear) coefficients — the two-mechanism story is the interpretability payoff

count_family.note: wrapper-level class choice: ZeroInflatedPoisson vs ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomialP — negbin when the POSITIVE counts are themselves overdispersed

p.note: NB variance power for ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomialP: 2=NB2, 1=NB1; only when count_family=negbin

maxiter.note: statsmodels default; the two-block likelihood often needs more — raise on ConvergenceWarning

invariances.why: unpenalized MLE is scale-equivariant, but fit_regularized's L1 penalty is unit-dependent and the joint two-block Hessian is fragile under badly-scaled columns — the hardest convergence surface in this family
both submodels are link-linear in their covariates; a monotone transform changes both fitted mechanisms
no missing-value mechanism in either likelihood block; rows must be complete in BOTH exog and exog_infl
requires pre-encoded design matrices for both submodels
assumes a two-part mixture: a degenerate point mass at zero (Bernoulli via logit/probit) mixed with a Poisson or NB2/NB1 count distribution — zeros are asserted to arise from TWO distinct mechanisms
twice the parameters of a plain count model, and the mixture is identified only through the zero-vs-positive contrast — needs enough rows AND enough positive counts to separate the mechanisms
both link-linear submodels extend beyond the covariate range; the mixture mean extrapolates as their composition

featureStats.why: observed zero share minus the Poisson-implied exp(-lambda-hat) — the single stat that justifies the second mechanism; a near-zero gap means the inflation component is unidentifiable ballast
variance/mean of the POSITIVE counts decides the count block: near 1 -> ZIP, well above 1 -> ZINB — dispersion and zero-inflation are separate diseases needing separate cures
the raw zero share bounds the inflation model's class balance — at extreme fractions the count block starves; at low fractions the mixture collapses

modelMetrics.why: the Vuong non-nested test of the ZI model against its plain counterpart — the honest 'did two mechanisms beat one' scoreboard, since the models are not likelihood-nested
the fitted pi's clustering near 0 means the structural-zero regime is vestigial (commit back to plain count); pi near the raw zero rate everywhere means the inflation covariates carry no signal

edgeCases.behavior: inflation block unidentified; pi -> 0 boundary, SEs blow up

edgeCases.condition: BFGS non-convergence of the joint likelihood
edgeCases.note: start_params from a plain count fit + zero inflation; raise maxiter
fit_regularized or shrink exog_infl to fewer columns

edgeCases.behavior: zero-inflation absorbs variance it shouldn't; biased pi

driver.constructor: ZeroInflatedPoisson(y, sm.add_constant(X), exog_infl=..., inflation='logit').fit(method='bfgs', maxiter=...) | ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomialP(..., p=2)
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant on both designs; predict(which='mean') for the score port and (1 - predict(which='prob-main'))  # pi = P(structural zero) = 1 - P(main regime) / inflation pi for the probability port; class switch on count_family

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling in either block; dropped rows distort the zero-vs-positive contrast the mixture is identified by
link-linearity in both submodels benefits from unskewing covariates
MLE is scale-equivariant, but the joint two-block optimization is the family's most fragile — standardization materially helps BFGS converge
both design matrices need categoricals encoded before fitting
